decision.explanation: Outcome: outside-reference evidence. Initial priorities were the reference-discriminating full-band spectral shape, dominant FFT families, band-envelope modulation and impulsiveness/time-frequency structure; all supplied available views were then checked. The decisive measurements are Q01's much higher spectral centroid (369.76 Hz versus 51.85–65.85 Hz), much greater spectral flatness, dominant 92/110/452 Hz components instead of the references' common 44–46 Hz dominance, elevated STFT/wavelet floors, and incompatible carrier-band modulation patterns [Q01.C01.S0001, D01.stft_detail, D01.wavelet, D01.envelope_1, D01.envelope_4, D01.envelope_5]. The strongest counterevidence is partial overlap near 30, 61 and roughly 105–110 Hz, plus R06 being nearest in the forced baseline and several descriptive controls; however, no acceptance threshold is supplied and the correlated views consistently show a different acquisition/spectral regime. Numeric measurements, not image proximity, drive the decision. Cyclic coherence is weak and broadly non-discriminating, while cepstral distances and isolated envelope-control minima conflict across references rather than supporting one condition [D01.cyclic, D01.cepstrum]. Orders and synchronous averages are unavailable because no independent RPM trace was supplied for Q01 or any reference [D01.orders, D01.synchronous, R02.orders, R02.synchronous, R03.orders, R03.synchronous, R04.orders, R04.synchronous, R05.orders, R05.synchronous, R06.orders, R06.synchronous, R07.orders, R07.synchronous, R08.orders, R08.synchronous]. Therefore no supplied condition has known similarity; fault identity, component, and severity are not established.
